items.title: Do only Mersenne primes have “good” permutations?
items.body:
Let $n>1$ be odd. Call a permutation $a_1,\ldots,a_n$ of ${1,\ldots,n}$ good if every proper consecutive block of length 2 or more has non-integer average.

The whole permutation must be excluded, since its average is $(n+1)/2$.

For every Mersenne prime $p=2^m-1$, the permutation

$$ 1,\ p-1,\ p,\ p-3,\ p-2,\ \ldots,\ 2,\ 3 $$

is good.

I ran a numerical search for odd $n\leq41$, and it yielded good permutations precisely for

$$ n=3,7,31. $$

Question. Does a good permutation exist for $n$, if and only if $n$ is a Mersenne prime?
